name: El Drago Milenario
age_estimate: disputed: a modern study puts it near 700 years, popular tradition says 1,000 years or more

location.address: Parque del Drago, Icod de los Vinos, Tenerife

access: Paid entry to Parque del Drago (a 3-hectare botanical park established 1996); the tree is also partly visible from outside the park but the full view is inside.
transport: Central Icod de los Vinos, walkable from the town's main square (a few minutes)
verify_notes: Species Dracaena draco, the largest and oldest known living specimen, declared a Spanish national monument in 1917. AGE IS GENUINELY CONTESTED AND SHOULD STAY THAT WAY: es.wikipedia cites current scientific estimate of approximately 700 years with a margin of error of 100-150 years (so roughly 550-850), while popular/tourist sources and tradition claim 800-1,000+ years, and some folklore claims go as high as 3,000 (unconfirmed, do not use as a fact bound). Dracaena draco has NO annual growth rings, so it cannot be dated dendrologically at all; do not attempt a girth-based derivation for this species. Height 18m (es.wikipedia) to 21m (other sources); trunk perimeter/girth about 20m at base; crown diameter approximately 20m; over 300 primary branches. Underwent 'profound sanitation' in 1985 (internal ventilation installed against fungal rot); the road running past it was relocated in 1993 to reduce vehicle pollution and vandalism risk. No evidence found this pass of recent storm damage or a lost branch; current status per sources is protected and stable, condition monitored (a health study ran Oct 2023-Mar 2024 per eldiario.es, informing conservation work). girth_cm: 2000 (20m perimeter, i.e. roughly 6.4m diameter at base, an unusually wide multi-stemmed base typical of the species, not a single narrow trunk).

name: Pino Gordo

location.address: TF-21, Vilaflor de Chasna (viewpoint near km 67, Corona Forestal), Tenerife

access: Free. Reached via a short (roughly 150-200m) marked trail from a signed parking/viewpoint area just off the TF-21 mountain road toward the Parador; benches and information panels on site.
transport: By car via TF-21 from Vilaflor village (a few km); no public transport reaches the viewpoint directly
verify_notes: Widely called the most voluminous tree in Europe of its kind. Height over 45m (one source: 45.12m); girth/circumference cited as 'nearly 10m' and, more precisely, 9.36m (thickest native tree in Spain) -- girth_cm: 936. Sits at over 1,400m elevation in the Corona Forestal Natural Park (NOT the ticketed core of Teide National Park, which only gates the cable car). Featured on Vilaflor's municipal coat of arms. Survived multiple wildfires and storms; bark shows fire scarring. Pin confirmed against an OpenStreetMap natural=tree node named 'Pino Gordo' on TF-21 in Vilaflor de Chasna matching the description exactly (a second, separate 'Pino Gordo' bus-stop node sits ~30m away at the parking area). Sits about 150m from Pino de las Dos Pernadas (tfe_003), so the two form one small walkable cluster at the same viewpoint.

name: Pino de las Dos Pernadas

location.address: TF-21, Vilaflor de Chasna (same viewpoint area as Pino Gordo), Tenerife

access: Free. On a small rise near the same signed viewpoint/parking area as Pino Gordo, with benches for viewing.
transport: By car via TF-21 from Vilaflor village; same stop as Pino Gordo
verify_notes: Called the tallest native tree in Spain: 56m tall. Girth about 8m (girth_cm: 800). Trunk forks into two thick limbs of similar thickness at around 10m height, which gives the tree its name (dos pernadas = two limbs/legs). Pin confirmed against an OpenStreetMap natural=tree node named 'Pino de las dos Pernadas' on TF-21, about 130-150m from the Pino Gordo node, consistent with descriptions of the two standing near each other on the same short trail. Same fire/storm history context as Pino Gordo (Corona Forestal Natural Park, free public access).

name: El Gran Ficus

location.address: Jardin Botanico de Puerto de la Cruz (Jardin de Aclimatacion de La Orotava), Calle Retama 2, Puerto de la Cruz, Tenerife
location.neighbourhood: El Botanico, Puerto de la Cruz

access: Paid entry to the botanical garden (around 3 euros), open daily 09:00-18:00, closed 1 Jan, Good Friday and 25 Dec.
transport: Central Puerto de la Cruz, walkable from town; local bus stop 'Jardin Botanico' right outside
verify_notes: Likely the Lord Howe Island form of the species (f. columnaris / var. columnaris, a form of Ficus macrophylla native to Lord Howe Island rather than mainland Australia); sources differ on how precisely to name the variety, use the species-level canonical name. DOCUMENTED PLANTING: planted by the garden's Swiss head gardener Hermann Wildpret during his tenure (1860-1893), specifically 'in the 1870s' per two independent secondary sources -- this is a real basis for a derived age (documented planting date for THIS specimen, not a bridge from the garden's own 1788 founding, which is much older and refers to the garden as a whole). One weaker source (getawayguide.co.uk) separately states 'around 200 years old' without giving a planting date; recorded as a conflicting figure rather than resolved. Height approximately 30m. Famous for its many aerial roots descending from the branches like columns, forming what visitors describe as a cathedral-like colonnade; some have thickened into secondary trunks. Spanish Wikipedia confirms the garden's own coordinates (28.4114N, 16.5358W) and founding by royal order of Carlos III, 17 August 1788, inaugurated 1792, but does not itself mention the ficus by name, so the garden-level Wikipedia entry is NOT being used as a source for the tree's own age. location_precision is approximate: coordinates given are the garden's own (OSM way centroid), not the specific tree's plot inside the ~20,000 sqm grounds; the tree is a can't-miss single specimen once inside and the garden is compact, but no tree-level coordinate was found this pass.
